1989-2000.what: The ground-floor windows are replaced by a shopfront: a fascia, a blank panel and a double door, with a signboard on the wall above.
1989-2000.why: The house was turned into a shop or business premises.

1989-2000.what: The small gable window gets a casing and a sill with feet where it was bare before.
1989-2000.why: A first step in renewing the windows, as in a repair run.

2000-2010.what: A glazed veranda with a balcony above is built onto the side wall facing the lane.
2000-2010.why: The owner expanded the premises, probably as the shop did well; this is new building, not repair.

2000-2010.what: The boards come off the attic window and the two ground-floor windows, and they are glazed and open again.
2000-2010.why: The house was reoccupied or repaired after standing empty.

2000-2010.what: Both windows on the gable end are boarded up with crossed planks.
2000-2010.why: The house was vacated and let go.

2010-2020.what: The big shop window and fascia are gone. Ordinary house windows stand in their place, lined up under the upper windows.
2010-2020.why: The shop closed and the ground floor went back to living use.

2010-2020.what: The two front windows get a lintel and a sill with feet, like the gable window already had.
2010-2020.why: The window renewal that began in the 1990s was carried on to the front.

A.claim: It was built as a house: the ground-floor windows and door line up under the upper windows. A shopfront with a big plate-glass window and fascia was cut into the ground floor at some point before 1989.
It was a shop for at least 1989 to 2010, and the roof, upper windows and walls stayed intact and well kept throughout.
Between 2010 and 2020 the shop closed and the shopfront was taken out for ordinary house windows, so the ground floor went back to living use.
The bay window on the upper floor looks like part of the original house; I see no sign that it was added or changed.

B.claim: In 1989 it was a plain, tidy dwelling with flower boxes and an ordinary front door.
It became a shop or business by 2000, with a new shopfront and signboard on its ground floor.
By 2010 it was extended with a glazed veranda and balcony, so the business or household was growing and money was going into it.
It was well kept in every year I see, with no damage and the roof and upper floor untouched.

C.claim: It is an old, plain house with a sound roof and walls in every year; its windows were simple and bare in 1989.
Its windows were renewed in stages: the gable window by 2000, the front windows by 2020. That reads as a steady owner doing a bit at a time.
It had no extensions and no change of use in these years; it stayed a family house.

D.claim: It stood empty and boarded up in 1989 and 2000, and had probably been vacant for some time before 1989.
Between 2000 and 2010 it was reoccupied or repaired: the boards came off and the windows were glazed again.
Since 2010 it has been lived in and looked after, with windows open and no further damage.
Its roof and structure kept sound even while it stood empty.

E.claim: It was a lived-in small house with open windows in 1989 and 2000.
Between 2000 and 2010 it was vacated and its windows boarded up.
It was still boarded and empty in 2020, so it has been let go for at least ten years.
It happens in the same decade that D is reoccupied. Residents may have moved from the top of the lane to D, but I only guess that.
